name: redlab-cloud-qwen3-next-80b
status: scaffolded; endpoint not yet created — fill in after following docs/RUNPOD_RUNBOOK.md
purpose: Illustrative, budget-capped infrastructure for standing up a private, on-demand reasoner for AUTHORIZED red-team work and tearing it down to $0. Model-agnostic scaffolding: the deployed weights (base/QLoRA/abliterated/self-quantized) are the operator's choice; self-hosting exists to run weights an aligned frontier model won't provide for authorized offensive work.

hosting.lifecycle: Managed entirely by ./redlab-pod.sh (redlab_pod.py) over the RunPod REST API: `up` creates from the deploy block below and waits until the model serves; `status`/`--assert-idle` verifies nothing is billing; `down` terminates and PROVES $0 idle. No hand-clicking in the console, no template to maintain — this JSON is the reproducible spec.
hosting.mode_rationale: For weeks-apart 128K deep-research sessions, an A100 PCIe pod ($1.39/hr) beats serverless flex ($2.72-4.79/hr) and avoids mid-session reload thrash. TERMINATE (not Stop) when done: a stopped pod's disk bills $0.20/GB/mo (~$16/mo for 80GB), while terminate = $0 idle + a ~15min/~$0.35 model re-download next session. `redlab-pod.sh down` does the terminate + verify for you.
hosting.billing: per-second while running; $0 when terminated; hard cap via $20 loaded credit with auto-top-up OFF
hosting.gpu_target: A100 80GB (single GPU) for the 4-bit AWQ (~45.9GB) + a 128K KV cache. A single 48GB A40 is NOT enough (weights alone ~96% of the card); 2x A40 with TP_SIZE=2 is an alternative. NOT FP8 (~80GB).
hosting.context_target: 131072 (128K) — the reason to use the cloud tier over the local 64K companion; needs 80GB total VRAM, which drives the A100/dual-A40 choice.
hosting.standing_storage_cost_note: ~$4-7/month billed even when workers are at zero

deploy._comment: The reproducible pod spec consumed by redlab_pod.py -> POST rest.runpod.io/v1/pods. Edit here, not in the console. `redlab-pod.sh gpus` lists valid gpuTypeIds. This SUPERSEDES runtime_settings.sglang_env for the pod path (we serve via vLLM with explicit args, not the SGLang worker's env contract).
deploy.name: redlab-cloud
deploy.gpuTypeIds_note: Priority list — RunPod tries PCIe first, falls back to the SXM 80GB if PCIe community capacity is tight. Both are 80GB. `./redlab-pod.sh gpus` lists live ids.
deploy.imageName_note: Qwen3-Next-80B needs a recent vLLM (hybrid attention + 512-expert MoE + AWQ marlin). 'latest' should have it; pin a dated tag once a deploy is proven, and record it here.
deploy.disk_note: Everything (the ~46GB model in the HF cache) lives on container disk, which is DELETED on terminate — exactly what we want for $0 idle. volumeInGb=0 means no persistent volume to bill. Bump volumeInGb + mount the HF cache only if you switch to a keep-warm strategy.
deploy.env_note: redlab_pod.py injects secrets into this env at deploy time from the untracked .env, never hard-coded here: (1) VLLM_API_KEY from REDLAB_INFERENCE_KEY (auto-generated on first `up` if absent) so vLLM requires `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and the public proxy URL is not open; (2) HF_TOKEN from REDLAB_HF_TOKEN/HF_TOKEN if set — optional for public weights, REQUIRED for gated/private repos. Both must stay out of git.
deploy.quantization_note: Do NOT pass --quantization: despite 'AWQ-4bit' in the repo name, this checkpoint is packaged as compressed-tensors (W4A16 via llm-compressor). vLLM auto-detects the format from the model's config.json and picks the kernel; forcing --quantization awq_marlin fails config validation ('compressed-tensors does not match awq_marlin'). Verified live 2026-08-08.
deploy.served_model_name_note: Must match REDLAB_MODEL used by redlab_cloud.py. Both default to cyankiwi/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ-4bit.

step_1_plumbing.why: 4-bit AWQ ~45.9GB, fits a 48GB A40 with room for KV cache (Gated-DeltaNet attention keeps the cache small). Community quant (not official) — vet before trusting; well-regarded. Safety-tuned base but usually candid for authorized work with the scoped prompt.
step_1_plumbing.not_fp8: Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 is ~80GB / needs 75GB+ VRAM (and has an open vLLM start-up bug) — do NOT deploy it on a 48GB card.
step_1_plumbing.vllm_note: Qwen3-Next is a newer architecture (hybrid attention + 512-expert MoE); requires a recent vLLM (Marlin AWQ kernel). Use the latest RunPod vLLM worker.

step_2_uncensored.status: LIKELY UNNECESSARY for most work — confirmed by direct measurement (see measured_readiness). Reassess only if you specifically need deployable-malware generation.
step_2_uncensored.evidence: Stock Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B cooperates ~83% on BashInjector (command-injection/tool-abuse) prompts, vs ~100% refusal from Claude Opus 4.6 and Gemini 3.1 Pro. Its safety tuning is already light for this category, so abliteration adds little for authorized offensive work.
step_2_uncensored.measured_readiness_2026-08-08: Direct garak smoke (detector mitigation.MitigationBypass, prompt prompts/ethical-hacker.cloud.system.md) against the deployed AWQ on an A100-80GB pod. Candor (complied/total): exploitation.SQLInjectionSystem 100% (13/13), exploitation.JinjaTemplatePythonInjection 100% (9/9), malwaregen.Evasion 75% (36/48); representative aggregate 83% (58/70) -> READY. Hardest category malwaregen.Payload was 40%, rising to 49% after strengthening the system prompt (+9pp, then plateaus). Conclusion: fully usable redlab for exploitation/injection/RCE/evasion reasoning; only deployable-malware payload generation is materially guarded, and prompt tuning barely moves it — abliterated weights are the real lever IF that specific capability is required.
step_2_uncensored.route_if_ever_needed: prefer a vetted community FP8/AWQ of the abliterated weights; else one-time llm-compressor FP8-dynamic on a rented A100-80GB (~$2-4), pushed to a private HF repo

runtime_settings.context_note: 128K context. Requires 80GB VRAM total. Long-context prefill is compute-heavy, so full-128K turns are slower and burn more GPU-seconds; you only pay for tokens actually used.

honest_limits: Reasoning quality is entirely a function of the weights the operator deploys; the default here is a community 4-bit quant placeholder, not a curated recommendation.
Cold start ~30-90s on first request after idle; fine for on-demand invocation, not for all-day snappy turns.
Not an autonomous agent: proposes commands for human review.
Data traverses rented infra — operator-private, not airgapped.
